headline: Stranded Tourist In Meghalaya Resolves Standoff By Offering Local Cab Driver A LinkedIn Recommendation
body:
Sumit Verma, a 28-year-old product manager currently stranded at the Assam-Meghalaya border, reportedly ended a four-hour taxi blockade this morning by promising to write a glowing LinkedIn recommendation for his driver, 44-year-old local operator Bikram Thapa, praising his 'exceptional strategic maneuvering in high-pressure transit environments.'

Verma, who had been unable to move his vehicle due to a territorial dispute between regional driver unions, decided to pivot from traditional pleading to corporate networking. 'I noticed Bikram was feeling undervalued because his permit doesn't technically cover the exact patch of asphalt we were parked on,' Verma explained while clutching his laptop. 'I told him if he gets me to Shillong, I’ll certify his skills in "Supply Chain Resilience" and "Conflict Resolution" on the global stage. He immediately moved his barricade.'

Thapa, who has been driving local routes for two decades, admitted the offer was too professional to ignore. 'I have never been offered a digital endorsement for my performance before,' Thapa said, signaling to his colleagues that the impasse was effectively resolved. 'Usually, it is just people yelling at me about the fare, but this man understands that my ability to block a road is actually a transferable soft skill in logistics.'

Local authorities have reportedly observed a surge in similar negotiations, with several tourists now opening their laptops at the border, attempting to leverage their corporate benefits to secure safe passage through disputed transit zones.
caption: When the taxi union blockade gets you down, just offer them a digital endorsement for their 'Aggressive Logistics Management' skills. It’s all about networking at the border. (satire) #Meghalaya #Assam #TravelTips #CorporateLife
